newsitem.title: ITALY: IMI willing to be holder in Paolo.
newsitem.headline: IMI willing to be holder in Paolo.

text.p: The board of investment bank IMI has authorised its executive committee to pursue negotiations which could lead to IMI becoming a core shareholder of San Paolo, IMI said on Tuesday.
IMI said in a statement the executive committee had been granted authority to carry on talks "aimed at the participation of the institute in agreements of stability ahead of the privatisation."

IMI, which currently holds a two percent stake in San Paolo, has an option which expires in June to raise its stake to five percent and thereby become one of a hard core of allies with significant shareholdings in San Paolo.
San Paolo, indirectly controlled by a foundation called Compagnia San Paolo, is moving ahead with plans to privatise ownership of the bank.
The Compagnia wholly owns a holding company called San Paolo Holding which in turns controls around 65 percent of the bank.
The aim is to reduce the Compagnia's stake in the holding company to around 25 percent by offering shares to the public and to a core of stable shareholders.
